paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar ben Dama, Yishmael’s sister’s son. He died in sanctity from a snakebite. Heilprin says he declined the use of Names and incantations on the wound [in the Bavli account, ben Dama asks to accept the offer and Rabbi Yishmael forbids it], Avodah Zarah, chapter 2. Some say a royal martyr instead of Yehudah ben Tema; see there. An account attributed to the Jerusalem Talmud calls the snakebite victim Yehoshua ben Dama, Yishmael’s sister’s son; see there. [The checked Jerusalem Avodah Zarah and Shabbat texts name Elazar.] This Elazar was killed wearing tefillin, still on his head. Shetei Hallechem: ben Dama asked Yishmael, “Having learned all Torah, may I learn Greek wisdom?” “Find a time neither day nor night.” Yuchasin’s Yesod Olam with Rema’s glosses calls him Zakkai’s colleague. This is false: Yishmael’s sister’s son, and Yishmael studied with Eliezer ben Hyrcanus, Zakkai’s student.
